    type: $type
    repo: $repo
    image: $image
    registryCredentialId: $registryCredentialId
    branch: $branch
    rootDir: $rootDir
    runtime: $runtime
    buildCommand: $buildCommand
    startCommand: $startCommand
    dockerfilePath: $dockerfilePath

renderReference.summary: The official docs describe canceling an in-progress deploy. Successful-release preservation in its failure section is qualified by “if any”; no authenticated Render confirmation wording was observed.

limits: The live copy failures are the canonical web-service deploy-detail caller at fresh390px and fresh1440px. List/Events, other resource kinds, aliases, Chinese and other browsers were source-traced or untested, not additional live failures.

The current create-trigger body passes. A live prior-release control preserves its exact public startup marker. This is the old103 resolution's explicitly deferred retry/unknown-context remainder, not a claimed regression of its create branch.

The first release used the native900s deadline and settled update_failed at16:08:32.238320Z. An initial post-verdict capture at16:09:09 still has one desired pod; zero desired replicas/no pods is observed by16:09:49 and retained at16:10:29 after public503s. Do not claim immediate zero or a full30-minute stopped observation.

After canceling the third bad attempt, one immediate read still showed Deploying and a terminating instance before the normal operator settle. Its canceled row/public503 and later Canceled acknowledgement are preserved; no instantaneous convergence is claimed.

An earlier manual-deploy click dispatched no TriggerDeploy and did not reproduce after a fresh load. Its unchanged single-row history was checked before a new user action. No duplicate writer, browser restart or resource recreation was used; no separate permission or silent-click finding is filed.

Three native DeployActions requests were aborted; one four-read batch and one asset preload have no completion status in the network capture. Request bodies identify them; their causes are not asserted. Other HTTP200 operations were not all body-audited.

Local node_modules contains older Radix1.1.15 and was excluded from the pinned-version explanation. Actual lock-resolved alert-dialog1.2.1/dialog1.3.1 cached sources were inspected; the production serving SHA/package set is not inferred.
No product code or tests changed, and no historical implementation suite was rerun for the filing. The observed exit42 and startup wait were intentional QA inputs, not bugs.
